name: Acrokeratoelastoidosis of Costa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Acrokeratoelastoidosis of Costa

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, firm, hyperkeratotic papules localized on the margins of the hands and feet
Histological evidence of fragmented and reduced elastic fibers (elastorrhexis) in the dermis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other keratodermas and elastin disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation of elastorrhexis with exclusion of other similar conditions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is not routinely available; diagnosis is primarily clinical and histological.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fragmented elastic fibers in the dermis
searchTerms: broken elastic fibers in skin layer

genetic: Possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern; no specific gene identified
other: Histopathology showing elastorrhexis with fragmented elastic fibers in dermis
Clinical examination revealing characteristic acral papules

distinguishingFeatures: Punctate keratoderma lesions primarily on palms and soles without elastorrhexis
Lack of elastic fiber fragmentation on histology
Serpiginous, transepidermal elimination of abnormal elastic fibers
Lesions often on neck and face rather than acral margins
Localized keratotic lesions without elastic fiber abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of secondary infection (e.g., purulence, increased pain)
Systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
references: Costa OG. Acrokeratoelastoidosis. Arch Dermatol Syphilol. 1953;67(3):284-289.
Rothman A, et al. Acrokeratoelastoidosis: clinical and histopathologic features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 1980;3(2):169-174.
